newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open cautiously, expected firmer.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open cautiously, expected firmer.

text.p: A cautious opening to Friday's trading session on the Singapore stock market reflected an overnight fall on Wall Street, but expectations are that share prices would remain firm, dealers said.
"Singapore opened cautiously on the overnight Wall Street correction, but we expect firmness today," one dealer said.
New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average had closed down 11.55 points at 6,418.47 on Thursday. Singapore's Straits Times Industrials Index was down 0.96 point at 2,196.73 at 0215 GMT.
Early trade saw some profit-taking, but dealers said they expected it to be absorbed by confident buying.
At 0210 GMT, gainers were ahead of losers by 94 to 71 on volume of 42.22 million units.
Trade in the opening hour saw shares in the Jardine empire move up sharply on healthy volumes.
At 0215 GMT, Hongkong Land Holdings was up U.S.$0.15 at US$2.93, Jardine Strategic Holdings had gained US$0.24 to $3.45, and Jardine Matheson had risen US$0.35 to US$6.60.
Dealers said the moves were linked to speculation surrounding a rumoured property deal in Hong Kong that was expected to prove positive for the Jardine group.
